subproblem.title: A scalar multiple of a boundary is supported in the support: S = c·∂T ⇒ spt S ⊆ spt T
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P (U : Set (Euclid P)), T ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U) and S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U (n+1), GeometricCurrentOn U n) and c ∈ ℝ. If S(ω) = c·∂T(ω) for every test n-form ω in U (∂T = T.boundary, ∂T(ω) = T(dω)), then spt S ⊆ spt T (GeometricCurrentOn.support, Simon 6.2.11).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (c : ℝ), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = c * T.boundary ω) → S.support ⊆ T.support
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 (a) and Step 7 of the parent proof ("if B vanishes on an open O with compact closure, so does ∂B ... and hence Z = c·∂B"; "spt X ⊆ spt Y: if O is open with compact closure and Y vanishes on O, then so does X = Y.boundary"), stated once for an arbitrary constant c.
Notation. For a current V ∈ 𝒟_j(U), its zero region Z(V) (GeometricCurrentOn.zeroRegion) is the union of all sets W such that W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U, and V vanishes on W (V.VanishesOn W: V(η) = 0 for every test j-form η in U with tsupport η ⊆ W). By definition spt V = U ∖ Z(V) (GeometricCurrentOn.support).

1. Let W be one of the sets whose union is Z(T): W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U, and T(η) = 0 for every test (n+1)-form η in U with tsupport η ⊆ W.
2. Let ω be a test n-form in U with tsupport ω ⊆ W. The test (n+1)-form dω := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U n ω has underlying form exteriorDerivative ω, and tsupport(dω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W by tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset. Hence T(dω) = 0 by step 1.
3. By the hypothesis and GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply (∂T(ω) = T(dω)), S(ω) = c·∂T(ω) = c·T(dω) = c·0 = 0. Since ω was arbitrary, S vanishes on W; W has the required openness and compactness properties, so W is one of the sets whose union is Z(S), i.e. W ⊆ Z(S).
4. As W was an arbitrary member of the family defining Z(T), Z(T) ⊆ Z(S). Therefore spt S = U ∖ Z(S) ⊆ U ∖ Z(T) = spt T. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take W in the family defining the zero region of T (open, relatively compact in U, T vanishes on W).
For a test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W, tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, so T(dω) = 0 and S(ω) = c·T(dω) = 0.
Hence W lies in the zero region of S; so zeroRegion T ⊆ zeroRegion S and spt S = U ∖ zeroRegion S ⊆ U ∖ zeroRegion T = spt T.

audit.reason: The statement and type agree, including arbitrary U and c. Exterior differentiation preserves test-form support, so every set defining T.zeroRegion also defines S.zeroRegion. Taking relative complements proves the required support inclusion without circularity.
